assumptions: The candidate is evaluated as the stated standalone release-gate SaaS for small Polish installation contractors, not as an unpriced enterprise consulting engagement.
The contractor or its accountant retains final invoice-submission authority and grants only the KSeF rights required for the selected connector workflow.
The proposed pricing, gross margins, customer count, and eight-to-ten-year founder-wealth path are planning scenarios rather than observed performance.
The competitor pages accurately describe currently offered features and list prices, although they do not establish incumbent adoption, reliability, or customer satisfaction.
The parents' installer can provide genuine workflow cases but cannot by itself establish independent willingness to pay or representative market frequency.
The relevant population of installation firms with contract-governed evidence gates is materially narrower than the cited broad construction-enterprise denominator and remains unknown.
Mandatory KSeF continues substantially as described and its production interface remains publicly documented and accessible subject to customer-granted permissions.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Obtain several independent paid pilots that quantify baseline and post-product days-to-invoice, missing-evidence exceptions and dispute losses; demonstrate a task competitors cannot reproduce with configuration alone; validate willingness to pay at a margin-supporting price, repeatable onboarding hours and support load, retention intent, a relevant customer denominator, and a written partner channel with credible CAC and payback.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: The opportunity correctly identifies a real boundary in the mandatory workflow: KSeF cannot carry contracts, acceptance protocols, or unstructured site evidence, so those artifacts must be assembled upstream before an invoice is released. Contract-configured evidence rules could be a sharper control point than transmission alone, but the insight is only moderately distinctive because current field-service products already connect signatures, photos, protocols, milestones, invoices, and KSeF.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Missing or late field evidence can plausibly delay invoicing and create disputes, and incumbent messaging independently indicates that contractors experience paperwork-to-invoice friction. However, no representative frequency, delay cost, dispute cost, independent paid pilot, or willingness to pay for contract-specific gating has been observed; free Ministry tools solve basic compliance and Majsta's low price shows that customers can obtain much of the broader workflow cheaply.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Paid onboarding plus recurring software revenue could fund configuration and eventually support attractive software gross margins if one trade template onboards repeatedly without founder work. The current plan instead assumes only 55-70% pilot gross margin, faces an incumbent price anchor of PLN 39-89 per month, and needs roughly 4,700 customers under its own founder-wealth scenario; CAC, churn, support load, payback, and the claimed mature margin are all unmeasured, while contract-specific setup may preserve service intensity.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Polish renewable-energy, HVAC, and electrical contractors with two to twenty field workers and milestone-dependent invoicing form a coherent beachhead, and the founder has unusually cheap access to one relevant installer. Yet the cited construction-enterprise count is far broader than the payable segment and gives no evidence on worker count, contractual complexity, software spend, or reachable installation firms, so neither the required customer count nor an economically meaningful initial segment is established.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: Serwis Pro targets the same installation trades with offline signed protocols, photos, invoicing, FA(3) submission, and UPO, while Majsta spans signed offers, milestones, photo reports, acceptance protocols, and KSeF at very low prices. No exclusive channel, protected permission, proprietary standard, or demonstrated performance edge gives this entrant a credible route to a dominant position; the narrower release-rule wedge remains a hypothesis incumbents could add.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: If a reusable evidence-rule engine succeeds in one installation trade, similar contract-to-invoice controls could extend to adjacent field-service trades, bookkeeping offices, and embedded accounting or field-service integrations. Expansion is plausible rather than proven, and Poland-specific tax behavior, trade-specific templates, and the absence of a won beachhead limit how much optionality should be credited now.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: A corpus linking contract clauses, accepted milestone evidence, VAT treatments, exceptions, and invoice outcomes could eventually improve templates and create workflow switching costs. At present there is no proprietary corpus, exclusive data access, signed distribution, or hard-to-obtain right; the KSeF API, OpenAPI contract, environments, and libraries are public, and established workflow vendors can reproduce generic templates and release checks.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: The proposed contract-aware gate could be valuable if it demonstrably prevents incomplete invoice releases and shortens days-to-invoice. No comparative result currently shows better speed, fewer disputes, higher acceptance, stronger auditability, or lower total cost than Serwis Pro or Majsta; the planned PLN 99-249 monthly price is also above Majsta's PLN 39-89 while the incumbents advertise broader workflows.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: Mandatory KSeF receipt and issuance create a current workflow-change window, and the reported scale of early usage confirms that adoption is operational rather than distant. Momentum is tempered because basic functionality is free, public integration infrastructure lowers entry barriers, no KSeF-error sanctions apply in 2026, and direct competitors have already launched relevant end-to-end offers.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: The parents' installer is a credible low-cost design environment and can support concrete case mapping without cold acquisition. It is not independent demand evidence, and the proposed bookkeeping-office, wholesaler, and software-vendor channels have no written commitments, conversion data, commissions, or CAC; acquiring thousands of low-ARPA contractors would be difficult without a repeatable partner motion and would otherwise conflict with the founder's preference for bounded social and support work.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: A narrow human-approved MVP is technically plausible within the stated capital and part-time limits, and schema validation, exception classification, and workflow automation fit the founder's skills. Scaling requires secure handling of taxpayer-granted permissions and certificates, reliable offline and exception behavior, tax and contract-domain accuracy, support discipline, and proof that configuration does not become custom consulting; those risks are manageable for a pilot but material for a 4,700-customer business.

highest_value_structural_change: Move upmarket from a generic low-ARPA contractor app to a contract-to-cash control layer for multi-crew installers and subcontractors with high-value milestone invoices, pricing substantial onboarding and recurring fees around configurable evidence matrices, dual approval, audit trails, and existing ERP or field-service connectors only after pilots prove material delay or dispute savings.
main_structural_strength: A real mandatory workflow boundary exists because KSeF excludes contracts, acceptance protocols, and unstructured site evidence, leaving a potentially valuable human-approved bridge from field completion proof to invoice release.
primary_score_limiter: There is no evidence that contract-specific evidence gating creates enough incremental paid value over low-priced end-to-end incumbents to support the proposed pricing, margins, retention, or required customer scale.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Majsta publicly offers signed offers, milestone schedules, photo reports, acceptance protocols, and direct KSeF for PLN 39-89 per month, while Serwis Pro offers offline signed protocols, photos, and KSeF to the exact installation audience.
